nature.com/sfts-virus

gov.uk/severe-fever-with-thrombocytopaenia-syndrome

News.title: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS)
News.content:
Key facts

SARS is a viral respiratory illness caused by the SARS-associated coronavirus

The illness was first reported in late February 2003 in China

The 2003 global outbreak spread to 29 countries, resulting in 8,096 cases and 774 deaths.

It is a respiratory virus that can spread through the air and via contaminated surfaces

There have been no reported cases of the disease since 2004

Overview

Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) is a viral respiratory disease caused by a SARS-associated coronavirus. Most people who contracted it were previously healthy people between the ages of 25 and around 70. The first cases were in China in November 2002 before the disease spread around the world.

The SARS outbreak was the first severe and readily transmissible new disease of the 21st century and demonstrated the world’s interconnectedness by travelling on international travel routes. The global outbreak was contained by July 2003.

Signs and symptoms

The incubation period for SARS was typically two to seven days, but could be as long as 10 days. The first symptom was generally a fever.

Other symptoms included:

Headache

Malaise

Muscle pain

Mild respiratory symptoms

Some patients reported diarrhoea during the early stages.

After three to seven days, a lower respiratory phase began with the onset of a dry, non-productive cough or shortness of breath.

Dangers and complications

In 10 to 20 per cent of cases, the respiratory illness was severe enough to require intubation and mechanical ventilation. The case fatality rate among people with a confirmed case of the disease was estimated to be around 9.6 per cent.

Transmission

SARS is an airborne virus that spreads through small droplets of saliva, similar to how the common cold and influenza spread. It can also spread indirectly via surfaces touched by someone infected with the virus. An investigation by the World Health Organization showed that it may also have spread via inadequate plumbing systems in apartment buildings. Virus droplets may have entered apartments via strong extractor fans.

Treatment

There is no cure or vaccine for SARS. Antivirals were not shown to be effective during the outbreak and treatment was supportive and based on the patient’s symptoms, for example the administration of oxygen and intravenous fluids.

Prevention

Controlling outbreaks relies on containment measures, including:

Rapid detection of cases through good surveillance networks and early warning systems.

Isolation of suspected or probable cases.

Tracing to identify the source of infection and contacts of those who are sick.

Quarantine of suspected contacts for 10 days.

Exit screening for outgoing passengers from areas with recent local transmission.

Disinfection of aircraft and cruise vessels using WHO guidelines.

Personal preventive measures include frequent hand washing with soap or alcohol-based disinfectants. Those with a high risk of contracting the disease, such as health care workers, should use personal protective equipment, including a mask, goggles, and an apron. Household contacts should also wear a mask whenever possible.

History

The first cases of what would become known as SARS first emerged in the wet markets of Guangdong in 2002 when it is thought to have spilled over to humans from civet cats. However, the World Health Organization was not alerted to this new disease until February 2003. WHO issued its first global alert in March when a patient was hospitalised in Vietnam. However, as late as April that year Chinese officials were still covering up the scale of the outbreak.

The outbreak spread to 30 countries, with Hong Kong and Canada among the hardest hit, but by July 2003 WHO said it had been mostly contained.

SARS was a harbinger of what was to come during the Covid-19 pandemic as it spread quickly via international travel routes and exposed a lack of protective equipment for health care workers. Similar containment measures such as isolation of patients, contact tracing and mask wearing were also deployed.

Useful links

who.int/severe-acute-respiratory-syndrome

nlm.nih.gov/severe-acute-respiratory-syndrome

News.title: Seasonal Flu
News.content:
Key facts

There are around a billion cases of seasonal influenza annually, including 3-5 million cases of severe illness

It differs from pandemic flu in that it is caused by an already circulating flu virus, whereas pandemic flu is a new virus against which people have little or no immunity

It causes 290,000 to 650,000 deaths every year..

Flu is very infectious and can easily spread to other people, with people being more likely to give it to others in the first five days.

Overview

Seasonal influenza, or the flu, is a common respiratory illness caused by flu viruses. It’s widespread and most people recover without needing medical attention. However, it can be severe or even deadly in some cases. There are four different types of flu virus: A, B, C and D. A and B virus cause seasonal flu.

Flu A includes subtypes like A(H1N1) and A(H3N2), with A(H1N1) being the virus behind the 2009 swine flu pandemic

Signs and symptoms

Flu symptoms start suddenly and typically appear one to four days after infection. Most people recover within a week.

Common symptoms include:

High fever or chills

Aches and pains

Dry cough

Fatigue

Sore throat

Headache

Runny or stuffy nose

Some may experience stomach issues like vomiting or diarrhoea, especially children.

The cough can last for two weeks or longer, and not everyone with the flu will have a fever.

Dangers and complications

While most people recover, flu can be more serious in certain high risk groups and can lead to serious complications such as pneumonia and sepsis. It can also worsen the symptoms of people with chronic conditions.

Flu-related hospitalisations and deaths mostly affect high-risk groups:

People 65 and older

Pregnant individuals

Young children (especially under two)

Those with weakened immune systems

If you or your child shows severe symptoms, seek medical help immediately.

Transmission

Flu spreads easily through respiratory droplets when someone coughs or sneezes. It’s most contagious in the first five days. In cold climates, flu seasons peak in winter, but in warmer areas, it can spread year-round.

It can spread easily in crowded places such as schools and nursing homes

Treatment

Most people recover without special treatment. To ease symptoms:

Rest, stay warm, and drink plenty of fluids

Take paracetamol or ibuprofen to reduce fever and pain

Children may need specific dosages for comfort

Antibiotics don’t work for the flu, but antiviral medicines can help if started early, especially for high-risk individuals.

Prevention

The annual flu vaccine is given to certain high risk groups in the UK. While it is less effective in older people, it still reduces severity and complications.

Other prevention tips include:

Wash your hands often

Cover your mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing

Stay home if you’re sick and avoid contact with others

Avoid touching your face

Flu vaccines are updated routinely with new vaccines developed that contain viruses that match those circulating.

History

For many years flu was thought to be a bacterial infection and it was not until the 1930s that the first flu virus was identified.

There have been flu outbreaks and pandemics for many years, with the most well known and deadly in recent times being the 1918 Spanish flu pandemic. It swept around the world as troops came home at the end of the First World War and is estimated to have caused between 50 and 100 million deaths.

It was caused by the influenza A(H1N1) virus and, unlike many flu outbreaks, mainly affected healthy, young people. There were alarming complications such as sufferers turning blue as their bodies were starved of oxygen. Other less serious symptoms included explosive nosebleeds.

More recently, the A(H1N1) virus caused the 2009 swine flu pandemic, which is estimated to have caused around 280,000 deaths.

Seasonal flu vaccines are updated each year based on which strains of the virus are circulating.

gov.uk/seasonal-flu

nhs.uk/influenza

cdc.gov/influenza

News.title: ‘No money and no plan’ behind UK aid strategy, MPs warn
News.content:
The FCDO’s strategy unveiled “four essential shifts” in the UK’s aid partnership: from donor to investor, from international intervention to local partnerships, from providing grants to exchanging expertise, and from service delivery to capacity building.

But Sarah Champion, the chair of the International Development Committee, said the FCDO still needs to “explain what success will look like and how our external partners will be involved”.

“Currently, we only have the skeleton of the Government’s new approach to development spending,” she said. “Ministers still need to put flesh on the bones.”

She added: “The reality is, when done well, development spend doesn’t just directly help the poorest in the world. It also helps to prevent conflict, keeps people secure and prosperous in their homes, prevents migration and enhances our global reputation.”

The report criticised the continued use of the foreign aid budget to fund refugees living in Britain, calling it the “antithesis [of a] proactive and strategic approach to aid”. It also warned there has been very little clarity from the government on what it means by a shift from “international intervention to local leadership”.

Other gaps include where money should be spent. While the government said last month that Britain would no longer provide aid to G20 nations, it has since launched investment partnerships in several G20 countries, including South Africa and Indonesia.

There are also concerns about the FCDO’s shift from a “donor to investor”. The government says it will help developing nations in Africa and Asia to grow sustainably, while also supporting fragile and conflicted affected regions such as Sudan, Yemen, Syria and Gaza.

But the committee raised concerns about an over-reliance on the British International Investment (BII), the UK’s aid-funded development finance institution.

The organisation invests in lower income countries to stimulate their economies with a focus on jobs and livelihoods, but critics say it has a weak focus on poverty reduction, a lack of oversight, and funds projects without clear outcomes – including luxury hotels.

News.title: Carrick deserves full-time job after guiding Man Utd to brink of Champions League
News.content:
The Premier League weekend comes to a close at Old Trafford as Manchester United host Brentford. The reverse fixture was won by Brentford 3-1 at the Gtech Stadium back in September. Brentford raced into a 2-0 lead thanks to Igor Thiago’s double before Benjamin Sesko got a goal back for Manchester United, who then missed a penalty in the second half before Mathias Jensen secured the three points for Brentford in second half stoppage time. If Brentford were to win this evening, it would be their first league double over Manchester United since 1936/37.

Manchester United claimed an important victory away at Chelsea last time out as they look to return to the Champions League. They start the night in third, ahead of Liverpool on goals scored and Aston Villa on goal difference. A win tonight would put them on the verge of Champions League qualification.

“I have said it many times, I enjoy being here, I enjoy the role I am in,” Michael Carrick said. “We have had some good results, and we are in decent shape. There is a lot to go. We still want to keep improving. There are layers that we want to get to really. I will see. I keep saying the same things in front of you every week. There is only so much I can say in terms of that, but I have said it many times again. I enjoy being here. I love being here. It is a real privilege to be in the position I am, but thriving with the responsibility that we got. I am not sure to be honest [when he will get clarity on his future] and it is not something in terms of deadlines that I am really chasing. I think it will become clear when it is going to become clear, and I am here at the moment to help the team and help the club get results. And at the moment, we are doing all right. We can still keep pushing and getting better. So really, that is genuinely all I am focused on.”

Lisandro Martinez is still suspended but Harry Maguire returns from his ban. Leny Yoro could return having missed the win at Chelsea whilst Matthijs de Ligt is closing in on a return from a long-term back problem.

Brentford have drawn their last five league games, including three goalless stalemates. The visitors go into this game in ninth but would rise into sixth with a victory at Old Trafford this evening.

Sports.title: Casemiro ‘can’t hold back his tears’ in unseen emotional moment after Man Utd’s win over Brentford
Sports.content:
CASEMIRO was overcome with emotion after Manchester United’s win over Brentford.

Unseen footage has emerged showing the veteran wiping away tears at full-time.





The Brazilian midfield enforcer delivered a stunning man-of-the-match display as United sealed a 2-1 victory at Old Trafford, tightening their grip on third in the Premier League and edging closer to Champions League qualification.

Casemiro set the tone early, powering home a header after just 11 minutes.

But it was his all-action performance that truly stole the show.

The 34-year-old racked up a staggering 11 tackles, won 16 duels and made nine clearances, becoming the only player in the last two decades to hit all three of those numbers in a single Premier League match.



It marked another high point in what is shaping up to be an emotional farewell.

Back in February, Casemiro confirmed he will leave United when his contract expires this summer.

And the magnitude of that reality hit hard at the final whistle.

As he walked off the pitch to a standing ovation, the former Real Madrid star struggled to contain his emotions, clearly moved by the love from the Old Trafford faithful.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Speaking afterwards, Casemiro admitted the connection he feels at United has taken him by surprise.

He said: “I spent most of my career in Spain playing for Real Madrid, where I won many trophies.

“But here, in just a few seasons at Manchester United, I’ve felt something different, something deep enough to make a grown man cry.

“At Real Madrid, winning trophies was incredible. But here, even a single victory feels just as significant, like lifting a trophy in its own right.

“That connection with the fans… it’s powerful enough to move a grown man. That’s why I couldn’t hold back my tears.”



His recent form has even sparked calls from supporters for a dramatic U-turn on his departure.

But interim boss Michael Carrick insists the decision is already made.

Carrick said: “It’s pretty clear, from both sides, it’s pretty clear.

“It also shows how much it means to him. The clarity has helped everyone understand the situation.

“Credit to him, he’s given absolutely everything and had some big moments for us.”



In a bid to replace Casemiro and others, SunSport understands that Manchester United have scheduled a meeting this week to discuss the sale of players in the summer.

United officials intend to provide clarity on certain players’ futures to pave the way for smooth departures.

Those expected to be on the discussion table include Andre Onana and Marcus Rashford, as well as potential targets to replace the departing Casemiro.

Sports.title: Diego Simeone sends Arsenal warning over Julian Alvarez transfer pursuit as Gunners face three-way battle for £81m star
Sports.content:
DIEGO SIMEONE has warned Arsenal that they face a three-way transfer fight if they want to sign Julian Alvarez this summer.

Simeone, 56, seemingly confirmed that the Gunners are one of three clubs interested in signing Alvarez following swirling rumours about a potential exit.





The Atletico boss revealed that Arsenal will have to tussle with Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain to secure Alvarez’s services, but said he isn’t concerned about the European giants vying for his star player’s signature.

Asked about Arsenal’s interest, Simeone said: “I’m not inside Julian Alvarez’s head.

“But I understand it’s normal that an extraordinary player like Julian Alvarez is wanted by Arsenal, Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.

“It’s normal because he’s very good.”



Arsenal are thought to have long-standing interest in Alvarez, and explored a move last summer before signing Viktor Gyokeres from Sporting.

Alvarez will likely lead the line for Atletico tomorrow evening when they host Arsenal at the Metropolitano Stadium for their Champions League semi-final first-leg.

The Argentine leads the Spanish club for goals and assists this season, and has been particularly dangerous in Europe – racking up 14 goal contributions in 13 appearances.

Alvarez, 26, previously spent two years in the Premier League with Manchester City, but swapped the Etihad for Atletico in a deal worth up to £81m after growing frustrated by playing second fiddle to Erling Haaland.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Atletico would likely demand a fee in excess of what they paid for Alvarez if they were to let him leave this summer.

Barcelona are thought to be leading the race to sign the Argentine as things stand, but Alvarez has already shut down exit rumours, stating his focus is still very much on Atletico.

The World Cup winner said this week: “I try not to pay too much attention to them [transfer rumours] because something new comes out every week, new information, and I don’t waste my energy on that.

“Instead, I try to focus on what we’re doing. It’s the most important time of the season, and I want to be in good shape so I can help the team and do great things here.



“I can’t be constantly clarifying or denying things. I don’t give importance to what comes out on social media because it often becomes a snowball of lies.”

Sports.title: Premier League club announce SECOND stadium connected by bridge to 32,000-seat arena in historic European first
Sports.content:
BRIGHTON announced historic plans to build a SECOND stadium – and Europe’s first purpose-built women’s football ground.

The Seagulls opened their 32,000-seater American Express Stadium in 2011.





And now they are working on opening another one next door, dedicated specifically to their women’s team.

The new venue will have a minimum capacity of 10,000 and will be located at Bennett’s Field – with the two arenas connected by a new bridge.

Brighton hope to open the new stadium in time for the 2030-31 season, subject to planning permission, with designs well underway including underground parking.

Albion released artist’s impressions under the ‘Built For Her’ motto and reiterated their commitment to supporting women’s and girls’ football.

Brighton Women’s managing director Zoe Johnson said: “The prospect of a bespoke stadium, built exclusively for women’s players, staff and supporters, is incredibly exciting.

“It is a project that is the first of its kind in the UK and Europe, and one of only three in the world.

“It is something we are asked about constantly, and we have worked hard to reach this moment, so it is exciting now to share this news with the wider world.

“It will help us push forward our ambitions to compete consistently both domestically in the Women’s Super League, and also in European club competition, while helping us to attract key staff and grow a passionate fan base.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Brighton & Hove Albion WFC – whose squad includes 77-cap England star Fran Kirby – currently sit sixth in the WSL and play their home matches at Crawley’s Broadfield Stadium.

But their new stadium will be tailored specifically to female athletes with various features such as changing rooms and recovery spaces designed for women’s needs.

Albion chairman Tony Bloom added: “Since we announced our intention to build a stadium for the women’s team in Brighton and Hove, we have seen unprecedented interest locally, nationally and internationally.

“It is a significant further investment in our long-term vision for women’s football at Brighton & Hove Albion.



“A women’s stadium in the city is essential to the continued growth of the team.

“We strongly believe it will strengthen our ability to attract elite talent, help develop our younger players for the future, support the growth of our fan base and create a genuine sense of belonging around the women’s game.”

And chief executive and deputy chairman Paul Barber said: “Our new women’s stadium is a powerful statement of our ambitions and will be integral to driving further momentum for the growth of women’s and girls’ football, not just in the UK but across the world.

“With a capacity aligned to Women’s Super League regulations, the stadium reflects our clear belief in ‘right sizing’ the stadium to grow the fan base sustainably.”

Sports.title: My dad won World Cup and Ballon d’Or.. I quit football to become DJ Ronald and amass half a million followers from music
Sports.content:
RONALDO NAZARIO won football’s biggest prizes – but his son decided to go down a totally different path after initially looking to follow in his footsteps.

Instead of challenging for a spot in Brazil’s squad for the World Cup, which his dad won twice, Ronald has become a hugely successful DJ.





Ronaldo has gone down in history as one of the most deadly finishers of all-time, with his stunning form in front of goal allowing him to bag the Ballon d’Or in 1997 and 2002.

And Ronald, 26, looked destined to challenge for similar accolades when he earned a call-up to Brazil’s Under-18s for the 2017 Maccabiah Games.

But he then made a huge career U-turn, deciding to blast out tunes instead of causing defenders countless problems on the football pitch.

Ronald has gone on to build an army of fans since making the sensational switch – resulting in him now boasting 478,000 followers on Instagram.

The Milan-born DJ, who specialises in electronic and house music, has also seen his number of streams on Spotify move into the hundreds of thousands.

And he has got his dad’s approval despite choosing not to make his original football dreams come true.

Ronaldo, speaking to former Real Madrid team-mate David Beckham during a live stream in 2020, said: “He’s an amazing DJ and he’s in Brazil.

“It’s my fault, I used to play CDs all the time. He grew up seeing me playing lots of music and he became a DJ.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“He’s very good, he plays electronic music. In Brazil and everywhere they call him.



“Last year he played in Ibiza for three different clubs.”

But Ronald has managed to combine his two loves by putting on sets at huge football showdowns.

He was on the decks before Cruzeiro’s Brazilian Serie A promotion clincher against Vasco da Gama in 2020.

Hyping up 60,000 fans was among Ronald’s early career highlights, while his dad was also in the stands.

Ronaldo, 49, enjoyed spells with Cruzeiro, PSV Eindhoven, Barcelona, Inter Milan, Real Madrid, AC Milan and Corinthians during his glittering career.

Sports.title: Aaron Danks is little-known English coach who guards Bayern Munich’s ‘lucky cockatoo’ and takes charge for PSG clash
Sports.content:
AARON DANKS is the little-known English coach tasked with downing the Champions League holders.

Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany will watch tonight’s semi-final first leg against PSG from the stands due to a suspension.





The former Manchester City captain has ruled out copying Jose Mourinho‘s 2005 trick of sneaking into the Chelsea dressing room in a laundry basket.

He said: “I’m 1.92m tall. I can’t fit in a washing basket.”

That leaves Birmingham-born Danks, one of his four assistants, to take the lead on the touchline in Paris.

Danks, 42, worked with Jude Bellingham and Bayern’s Jamal Musiala as a youth coach in the England setup and took charge of two Aston Villa games as caretaker after Steven Gerrard was sacked at Villa Park.

The first was a 4-0 win over Brentford, but that was followed by a 4-0 defeat to Newcastle.

Danks worked with Kompany at Anderlecht but left for Villa, where he worked with Gerrard, Dean Smith and Unai Emery before being taken to Middlesbrough by Michael Carrick.

He was reunited with Kompany in Germany when the Belgian swapped Burnley for Bavaria in 2024.

Danks is Bayern’s set piece coach but also has the bizarre role of looking after the club’s ‘lucky cockatoo’.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Bayern players celebrate trophy wins with a small porcelain statue of a cockatoo, pinched from a restaurant in Munich, which Danks guards.

Kompany said of the setup: “Danksy already has experience; he spent some time on the sidelines in England.

“He also usually plays a more vocal role, both in training and in games. I have 100 per cent confidence in the staff and everyone else as well. I’ll be sitting somewhere in the stadium.

“The procedures are clear. I know when I’m allowed to do something and how I can support the team. I’m not involved in every part.”



Sporting director Max Eberl added: “Vincent has charisma and everything that goes with it.

“But all the groundwork is actually done behind the scenes by his colleagues on the coaching staff.

“As a result, everyone is on board with the philosophy and the things we want to implement, both defensively and offensively.”

Sports.title: Atletico vs Arsenal latest as Madrid hit with weather warning amid complaints about Metropolitano Stadium pitch
Sports.content:
ARSENAL fans heading to Madrid have been issued an urgent weather warning ahead of their huge European showdown against Atletico.

Meteorologists have flagged thunderstorms and heavy rain across the Madrid Metropolitan Area and Henares Corridor, raising fears of travel disruption in the coming days.





Supporters travelling to Spain are being urged to follow local media updates, stick to official advice and double-check all transport arrangements before setting off.

And the looming storm could add another twist to an already fiery semi-final clash between the Gunners and Diego Simeone‘s men.

Because once the action gets underway, Arsenal face a different kind of battle, on the pitch itself.

Boss Mikel Arteta takes his side into the lion’s den at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium on Wednesday night, where conditions have already sparked complaints this season.

Atletico have turned their 70,000-capacity home into a fortress, but rivals reckon they’ve had a helping hand.

Tottenham were left fuming after their last 16 clash in March, claiming the pitch had been heavily watered, causing players to slip on the slick surface.

Then Hansi Flick accused the hosts of leaving the grass too long before Barcelona’s quarter-final, allegedly to slow the game down.

Now Arsenal must be ready for more of the same.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Atletico boss Diego Simeone is a master of turning every detail into an advantage, while the hostile Madrid crowd will crank up the pressure.

Uefa rules insist the pitch must be kept in the “best possible condition”, with strict guidelines on grass length and watering.

The surface cannot exceed 30mm and must be cut evenly, while any watering must be communicated in advance.



But crucially, clubs ARE allowed to water the pitch shortly before kick-off, something Atletico could use to their benefit again.

Arsenal will be watching closely.

Away from the surface concerns, Arteta is still sweating over key injuries.

Defender Jurrien Timber remains sidelined with a groin issue and has yet to fully step up his training, a major blow heading into the crunch run-in.

There is better news on Eberechi Eze, who expects to be fit despite a recent scare against Newcastle.



But Kai Havertz looks set for a spell out, although the issue is not believed to be serious.

Sports.title: England star, 31, set to be released weeks before World Cup as he breaks down in emotional exit video after 10 years
Sports.content:
JOHN STONES broke down in tears announcing his exit from Manchester City.

The England defender, 31, will end his 10-year stay at the Etihad when his contract expires on June 30.



John Stones' Man City stats Here is Stones' Man City career by numbers... Appearances: 293 Goals: 19 Assists: 6 Champions League: 1 Premier League: 6 FA Cup: 2 Carabao Cup: 5 Club World Cup: 1 Uefa Supercup: 1

And it means he will become a free agent midway through this summer‘s World Cup.



Stones choked back tears as he said: “It’s been my home for the past 10 years and it’ll be my home for the rest of my life.

“I came as a kid and now I’m leaving as a man. Becoming a father, a husband, and on the pitch a very fulfilled player, living all my dreams and lifting all the things I came here to achieve.

“At the start of my career here I never would have thought I’d be in this position – firstly to achieve everything but also to love the bond with everyone. Every dream has been smashed out of the park.

“If you said to me I’d be playing at City, winning everything, the fans singing my name wherever we go in the world, I don’t think I would have believed you.



“The fans mean everything to me. I hope I have made them proud and they can relate to me as a person and a player – how I have represented the club and will do for the rest of my life.

In total he has won 16 major trophies for the Blues and will collect a SEVENTH Prem winner’s medal if they chase Arsenal down in the next few weeks.

Stones said: “I don’t think we would have been anywhere near as successful if it wasn’t for him.

“The first time I met him, I left that moment and knew it was what I wanted to do and where I wanted to be – playing under the best manager in the world.

“I’m so glad I was able to share so many incredible moments with him.”

Stones has been in and out of the treatment room throughout his time at City, with injuries limiting him to just four Prem starts this season.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho lined up for sensational Real Madrid return with Benfica boss preferred candidate of Florentino Perez
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO is Real Madrid’s preferred candidate to become their next manager, according to reports.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United boss only joined Benfica in September and he is yet to lose a game in the Portuguese top flight.





But the Special One could be set for a stunning return to the Bernabeu after The Athletic claimed Madrid chief Florentino Perez was targeting him up to replace Alvaro Arbeloa.

Mourinho spent three seasons with the Spanish giants between 2010 and 2013, guiding them to LaLiga and Copa del Rey glory.

Former Liverpool defender Arbeloa has been in charge since Madrid axed Xabi Alonso in January.

But Arbeloa has endured a mixed time in charge and Barcelona look likely to pip his side to the LaLiga title.

The report says long-serving chief Perez is driving the process for the club’s next boss and is the “main supporter” of Mourinho.

But some figures within the club are against bringing the Special One back to the Spanish capital.

Mourinho was a divisive figure at Madrid and left after a trophyless season in 2012-13.

But his high profile nature would bring publicity to the club, who have previously re-appointed former managers.

Madrid also re-hired Carlo Ancelotti in 2021, six years after he initially left the Bernabeu.

Mourinho has already faced Madrid three times with Benfica this season and was involved in some controversy.

He was sent off during their Champions League clash in February for protesting a decision not to send off Vinicius Jr.



The Portuguese boss later drew criticism with his comments about Vinicius after he accused Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni of racism.

Mourinho appeard to shift the blame to the Brazilian as he said: “When he was arguing about racism, I told him the biggest person [Eusebio] in the history of this club was black. This club, the last thing that it is, is racist.

‌



Lowe, who has twice resigned from his position with the Saints as he oversaw their relegation in 2005 and when Southampton Leisure Holdings went into administration in 2009, has become an outspoken political operator. The 68-year-old departed Nigel Farage's Reform Party to launch Restore, with the ambition to advocate for the deportation of illegal immigrants, protection of British culture and restoration of Christian principles.

‌



Posting on social media, Lowe outlined one of his positions. He said: "We should ban foreigners from claiming benefits, and remove migrants who are incapable of financially supporting themselves - use those many saved billions to slash tax for the British men and women keeping the economy running.

‌



"Restore Britain would do exactly that, and put our own people first. Finally." Former Blues and England star Terry appeared to emphatically lend his support to the position. In the comments, he said: "100% yes"

FIFA see Pope-style request for Gianni Infantino turned down by Canada READ MORE :

Arsenal learn PGMOL decision after Mikel Arteta's fury over VAR and Nick Pope incident READ MORE :

Ex-Millwall and Leeds United boss Dennis Wise stepped his support up a notch and also commented: "200%" The pair saw some pushback to their positions.

"Cool. The odds are that if John Terry and Dennis Wise support something, it's probably best to be on the opposite side to them. Thanks," said one social media user.

‌



"Strange that, they seemed like such lovely, caring characters," added another. "Two idiots," said a further X user.

View 2 Images John Terry and Dennis Wise lent their support to Rupert Lowe (Image: Instagram)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"Wonder how the usual 'ex-footballers should shut up and stick to football' crowd will feel about this," another put forward.

It is not the first time Terry has lent his support to one of the MP for Great Yarmouth's posts. The Chelsea academy coach appeared to agree with Lowe's hopes to ban the burqa.

Lowe was shut down in Parliament recently as he put forward his desire to ban foreigners from claiming benefits. He claimed £10.1billion of Universal Credit payments in 2024 were 'gifted to foreign nationals' and asked if the solution was to: “ban all foreigners from claiming any benefits, remove from our country migrants incapable of financially supporting themselves and hand that money back to taxpaying British men and women.”

‌



Andrew Western, Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Transformation, ridiculed Lowe's use of figures and highlighted the issues with his position. The Labour MP said: “The figure that he uses is a complete conflation, a significant overestimation and shows his ignorance if he does not understand that it is impossible to suggest that that money has all been paid directly to foreign nationals.

“The figure that he uses is drawn from the total number of households with a foreign national in and many of the individual claimants could in fact be British or Irish citizens."

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand invites football fans on dream World Cup experience
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand invites football fans on dream World Cup experience

Rio will be in Los Angeles where four fans and their plus ones will enjoy a once-in-a-lifetime football experience

View Image Rio Ferdinand

He may have retired from international football in 2013, but Rio Ferdinand is on his way to the World Cup - and he's teaming up with Airbnb to offer football fans a once-in-a-lifetime trip.

‌



The former England captain is attending his first tournament as a fan in 30 years, having been either a player or pundit at every tournament since 1998.

‌



Rio will be in Los Angeles where four fans and their plus ones will enjoy a once-in-a-lifetime football experience.

‌



The Ultimate Quarter-Final Getaway includes a three-night stay at an Airbnb in the heart of the city with a private chef service and the chance to meet Rio at a live recording of the ‘Rio Ferdinand Presents’ podcast.

Guests will go behind-the-scenes with the Manchester United legend and his co-hosts, Joel Beya and Ste Howson plus a special podcast guest. They will also attend a FIFA World Cup quarter-final match in the city.

Rio said: “ Football has been my life, and there’s no bigger stage than the FIFA World Cup.

‌



This summer’s a big one with Airbnb. We’re all about bringing fans closer than ever, proper access, big moments, straight from the US.

And for me, it’s something new – I’ll be experiencing a World Cup as a fan for the first time in over 30 years. I can’t wait to get started.”

As the final countdown begins, new Airbnb data has revealed that England and Scotland fans top the league for travel to the World Cup, driving an increase in searches by 301% in host cities.

‌



It also shows supporters are turning the tournament into a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for road trips across North America planned around matches. They’re planning to stop at three destinations and stay for an average of 15 nights.

Lisa Marçais, general manager, UKI, Northern Europe & MEA, at Airbnb, said: "As the FIFA World Cup 2026 approaches, UK fans are turning their trips into real adventures.

“Whether it's a neighbourhood stay near the stadium or exploring the local city through an Airbnb Experience - from street art walks to food tours - we help fans get closer to the game, the culture, and everything each host city has to offer.”

Article continues below

**To join Rio in Los Angeles, football fans can request to book The Ultimate Quarter Final Getaway for free from May 12 at 10am BST at ** http://airbnb.com/rioferdinand

Four spots are available for a three-night trip (July 8 to 11, 2026), each bookable for free, for one guest and a plus one. They will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

Sports.title: Two Atletico Madrid stars 'extra motivated' to destroy Arsenal's Champions League dream
Sports.content:
Two Atletico Madrid stars 'extra motivated' to destroy Arsenal's Champions League dream

Antoine Griezmann will play his final Champions League home game on Wednesday night before heading to Orlando City in the summer, while club captain Koke's future is also uncertain

View Image Antoine Griezmann (R) and Koke of Atletico Madrid are both desperate to go out with a bang

Atletico Madrid star Koke says saying goodbye with the Champions League will provide “extra motivation.”

‌



Veteran Koke, 34, is out of contract this summer while France superstar Antoine Griezmann will play his last ever Champions League game at the Metropolitano before he departs for Major League Soccer at the end of the season.

‌



It will mark the end of an era for this Atletico team but also a chance for Diego Simeone who is in the fourth Champions League semi-final of his 15 year reign. They have know-how and experience as well as a reputation for upsetting the odds and revelling in their tag as underdogs.

‌



There is certainly emotion around Griezmann’s farewell and, while Koke’s future is not decided, they will both be in the spotlight as they prepare for what could be one last dance.

Koke said: “Well, I think if Antoine can say goodbye with the Champions League it would be incredible for everyone and we have the same motivation. Beyond Antoine’s farewell, I think we all have the motivation to win the Champions League, right? Which is the most we can achieve.

“Beyond the fact that next year Antoine might not be here or any other teammate, I think in the end this is a team and we play to try to achieve the maximum and the maximum right now is the Champions League.

‌



Julian Alvarez to Arsenal transfer bombshell dropped by Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone READ MORE :

Arsenal learn PGMOL decision after Mikel Arteta's fury over VAR and Nick Pope incident READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“I feel like I'm enjoying this season a lot, that Champions League semi-finals aren't played every year. We talked about it in the other press conference when we were in Al-Bassa. If we got to the semi-finals it was the seventh time Atletico Madrid had done it and luckily this is my fourth that I can play.

“So, it’s not played every year, enjoy it to the fullest. I don't know if I'll play one more but it is true that I'm going to enjoy it like I did the previous times.”

‌



Koke himself is still going strong but says he cope with the physical demands of the Champions League and feels as fit as ever which he also says stops him from looking back.

Koke added: “It doesn't surprise me, the truth is obviously as you get older it costs more, as happens to all footballers, but it doesn't surprise me.

“The truth is every day it motivates me more to be here, to be able to work as I've been doing all these years and honestly that motivation is what leads me to the level I'm giving during this season. The past is in the past and we have to enjoy it.

Article continues below

“I mean, I don't notice anything strange or that anything different is going to happen compared to other semi-finals, except that we're playing against a great team like Arsenal and it's a Champions League semi-final and with the greatest motivation, so nothing different changes or at least I perceive it as nothing different.”

Sports.title: Man Utd's ideal Casemiro plans with £131m double transfer swoop pushed
Sports.content:
Man Utd's ideal Casemiro plans with £131m double transfer swoop pushed

Casemiro announced he will leave Manchester United at the end of the season

View 2 Images Casemiro is heading out of Manchester United this summer (Image: Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Louis Saha believes Manchester United will need two players to fill the void left by Casemiro's departure. The former United striker has identified Aurelien Tchouameni and Bruno Guimaraes as the ideal pair to succeed the Brazilian.

‌



Casemiro confirmed in January that he would be leaving Old Trafford at the end of the 2025/26 season, bringing the curtain down on a four-year spell at the club. His exit will be deeply felt after he added yet another goal to his already impressive tally in United's 2-1 victory over Brentford on Monday night.

‌



That takes Casemiro's contributions to 11 in all competitions this season, and 40 in total. Saha knows only too well the weight of expectation at Old Trafford, and is convinced two quality replacements will be essential this summer.

‌



Speaking to BetVictor Online Casino, the 47-year-old said: "If you lose someone like Casemiro, you need experience and someone who can maintain the level in midfield. Guimarães would fit really nicely because he already knows the Premier League.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Gary Neville spots what isn't right at Man Utd as Michael Carrick backed to take action READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford transfer conditions emerge as Man Utd haggle with Barcelona READ MORE :

"He's aggressive but also very technical and can add goals. Tchouaméni has experience at the highest level and plays under pressure every day - that's very similar to what Casemiro brought. From those options, I would choose Guimarães and Tchouaméni."

‌



United have repeatedly been linked with Guimaraes ahead of the summer transfer window, with Newcastle anticipated to offload several key figures should they miss out on European football. Boss Eddie Howe previously played down any interest in his star players, but the midfielder's latest outburst following defeat to Arsenal will have put United's hierarchy firmly on high alert.

Reports indicate that the club have already held discussions with Guimaraes' representatives, with a fee of £60.8million being mooted for his signature. United consider this figure manageable, though he is far from the only midfield target on their radar.

Real Madrid's Tchouameni is another name in the frame as the club looks to mount a successful return to European competition next season. The 26-year-old has been linked with a £70m switch to Old Trafford this summer.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes is a long-term target for the club (Image: Lee Parker - CameraSport via Getty Images)

The Telegraph reports that the La Liga giants would be willing to sanction Tchouameni's departure, provided they can secure one of their own midfield targets first. Landing both players could prove a tall order for United, but Saha made abundantly clear that a significant investment will be required to adequately replace Casemiro's commanding presence.

Supporters are reluctant to see the Brazilian leave, with chants of 'one more year' echoing around the ground during recent fixtures. During United's victory over Brentford, Casemiro was spotted 'conducting' the crowd as they serenaded him following his opening goal.

Article continues below

The midfielder has just two matches remaining at Old Trafford and has worn his heart on his sleeve as the clock winds down. With such an influential figure heading for the exit, United face a monumental task in finding a replacement capable of matching his goals and overall contribution to the squad.

Sports.title: Paul Gascoigne's best-selling memoir is being translated in countries around Europe
Sports.content:
Paul Gascoigne's best-selling memoir is being translated in countries around Europe

'Eight' is short-listed for Sports Book of the Year 2026 and is being translated initially into Dutch and Polish. Talks are ongoing to sell the book in Italian and Danish.

Jeremy Armstrong interviews footballing legend Paul Gascoigne

Gazza's best-selling memoir will soon be translated into different languages just in time for the World Cup - and the England legend's birthday.

‌



'Eight' has just been short-listed for Sports Book of the Year 2026 and is being translated initially into Dutch and Polish. Talks are ongoing to sell the book, published by Reach Sport, in Italian and Danish. Paul, who turns 59 next month, has had his own language problems in the past.

‌



The book gives a compelling account of his life as a footballer and his time fighting addiction once his career was over. In an interview with the Mirror last year, he admitted that he had never been able to win his battle with the booze.

‌



View 3 Images Paul Gascoigne pictured in Poole, Dorset (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

He was just 21 when he signed for Tottenham Hotspur in 1988 for £2.2m, which was then a British record fee. He joked that his Spurs team mates struggled to understand his Geordie accent.

He told the Mirror: "No one at Spurs could understand a word I was saying. They had to get Chris Waddle to translate for me at training. It was really embarrassing."

‌



View 3 Images Paul Gascoigne was in a relaxed mood for his interview with the Mirror (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Fellow England star Waddle was also from Gateshead, Gazza's hometown. And Paul had the same issue on the Italian version of 'I'm a Celebrity' in 2021 when fellow contestants couldn't understand him either. He had to use the Italian he learned during his spell with Lazio in the 1990s.

But even that was a struggle. He described Italia '90 as the high point of his fame.

‌



But he is also brutally honest about the lows in his book, including his 2010 bid to 'save' fugitive killer Raoul Moat when Moat was cornered by police in Rothbury, Northumberland. It was a moment captured live on TV while Gazza was high on cocaine.

View 3 Images England legend Paul Gascoigne with Mirror reporter Jeremy Armstrong (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Paul told how he came 'back from the dead' when doctors restarted his heart in rehab - and how that was the lowest point of his life. The former England star was admitted to a clinic in Arizona in 2013 after celebrity stars including Chris Evans, Alan Shearer and Danny Baker rallied round to help him.

Article continues below

He was in an induced coma for 18 days and had an injection into his heart which doctors said had kept him alive. The rumours of his death were so widespread that when he returned to his native Tyneside, a woman stopped in the street in front of him and told him 'I thought you were dead'.

He admitted that he had never been able to win his battle with addiction to alcohol, but he had come to terms with his situation. The autobiography section of the sports book awards is decided by public vote.

To 'vote for Eight' go to: https://sportsbookawards.com/vote/

Sports.title: Real Madrid make Jose Mourinho their No.1 target to be manager next season
Sports.content:
Real Madrid make Jose Mourinho their No.1 target to be manager next season

Jose Mourinho is the man Real Madrid want to be their next manager with Florentino Perez leading the charge to hand the Special One a second spell at the Bernabeu

View 2 Images Benfica boss Jose Mourinho is on Real Madrid's radar (Image: Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images)

Real Madrid have made Jose Mourinho their top target to replace Alvaro Arbeloa this summer with president Florentino Perez driving the plan to bring the Special One back to Spain.

‌



Mourinho was in charge at the Bernabeu for three years from 2010 and won La Liga in record breaking fashion as well as the Copa del Rey. On both occasions he had to topple the juggernaut that was Pep Guardiola's Barcelona side.

‌



Arbeloa was hired to replace Xabi Alonso midway through this season, but will finish the campaign trophyless, leading to inevitable change. Perez allowed general manager Jose Angel Sanchez to lead their pursuit of Alonso, but will now take a central role in appointing their next manager, reports the Athletic.

‌



Mourinho has not been the serial winner he was when Real hired him 16 years ago, but is set to finish the season unbeaten with Benfica, even if they are set to miss out on the Portuguese title.

The 63-year-old only joined Benfica in September and is under contract until June 2027. However that agreement includes a clause in the region of €3million, allowing either party to break the deal up to 10 days after the final match of this season.

Jude Bellingham's reason for snubbing Man Utd transfer despite private tour of Old Trafford READ MORE :

Mourinho, who masterminded a win over Real in this season's Champions League, would have to take charge of a Los Blancos team that look poised to go a second year without a trophy. Perez is banging the Mourinho drum, but other voices within the club aren't so sure about his return.

‌



He left Madrid in acrimonious circumstances after taking on some of the club's leading figures. His comments proved divisive and there were well documented tensions with then-captain Iker Casillas, which did not endear him to some fans and the media.

This season he was critical of Vinicius Jnr, one of the team's leading lights, suggesting he incited an incident which ended with the Brazilian alleging he was racially abused by Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni.

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho claimed multiple trophies when he was last at Real Madrid

‌



It has become common in recent years for Madrid to appoint managers who have previously been at the club. Carlo Ancelotti is a successful example with the Italian returning from Everton in 2021 - six years after leaving. His second stint saw him complete two La Liga-Champions League doubles.

Former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp is another major name to be linked with the Real job. He's currently taken a lead role with Red Bull, but would be open to a coaching return. Mauricio Pochettino, Julian Nagelsmann and Didier Deschamps are three international coaches who could be available post-World Cup.

Sports.title: Barca want second Rashford loan deal
Sports.content:
Barcelona are interested in a second season-long loan deal for Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford.

The Spanish giants have the option to buy the on-loan 28-year-old permanently this summer for £26m but financial circumstances mean they are reluctant to trigger it.

Sky Sports News has previously reported Man United have no intention to renegotiate the fee agreed.

Barcelona are therefore considering making another loan proposal when talks renew at the end of the season.

The Spanish club's interest in signing Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid is also likely to be a factor in their squad planning.

Rashford is under contract at Old Trafford until the summer of 2028.

He has scored 12 goals and got 9 assists for the La Liga leaders this season.

Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone confirmed Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal's interest in Alvarez, who has scored 48 goals in 104 games for Atletico Madrid since his £82m move from Manchester City.

"I'm not inside Julian Alvarez's head," he said when asked about reports linking him with the Gunners.

"I understand it's normal that an extraordinary player like Julian Alvarez is wanted by Arsenal, Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona. It's normal because he's very good."

Sports.title: AIG Women's Open prize pot increased to $10m
Sports.content:
The R&A will increase the official prize fund for the 2026 AIG Women's Open for the sixth consecutive year, with the world's best players set to battle it out at Royal Lytham & St Annes in July for a slice of a $10m (£7.43m) pot.

Mark Darbon, the chief executive of the R&A, also revealed that the 2028 edition of the AIG Women's Open will be held at Sunningdale's Old Course, with Royal St George's set to host the 2027 event.

"We know Sunningdale will provide an outstanding venue in two years time," Darbon said.

"It will be the fifth time the championship has been held there and the first since 2008."

Officials have added an extra $250,000 (£185,651) to the purse this year following the success of the 2025 AIG Women's Open, where Miyu Yamashita claimed a two-shot victory over Charley Hull and Minami Katsu to secure her first major title.

This year will also mark the 50th anniversary of The AIG Women's Open. Jenny Lee Smith was crowned the tournament's inaugural champion in 1967, and the prize fund had stood at $673.31 (£500).

Broadcast coverage of the 2026 AIG Women's Open is also due to significantly increase, with fans able to watch 20 per cent more coverage throughout the week, which will be live on Sky Sports.

Early broadcast windows for rounds one and two will provide fans with a look at how the early starters are faring at Royal Lytham & St Annes, while morning marquee groups will also be shown between 9am and 1pm, while full main coverage will commence from 1pm to 7pm - every day from July 29 to August 2.

"Our broadcast coverage is fundamental to that ambition and with a with a 20% increase in live hours compared to 2025, we are setting a new benchmark for women's golf," Darbon said.

"The AIG Women's Open now delivers more linear television broadcast hours in the UK and US than any other women's golf championship, giving fans unprecedented access to the very best players in the world. This is another important step forward as we continue to invest in the Championship and grow its global audience."

Sports.title: Stones to leave Man City this summer
Sports.content:
John Stones has announced he will leave Manchester City at the end of the season.

Stones will follow another club legend, Bernardo Silva, through the exit door this summer as a free agent upon the expiry of his contract as City prepare for another big summer of change.

The England defender's final season at City has been hit by injuries which have restricted him to just four Premier League starts – but he leaves with a legacy of being one of Pep Guardiola's most important signings.

Stones was the second arrival under Guardiola, joining City from Everton for £47.5m in the summer of 2016, and has enjoyed a trophy-laden decade at the Etihad.

The 31-year-old has lifted 19 major trophies at City, including six Premier League titles, one Champions League, two FA Cups, five Carabao Cups and was part of the treble-winning side in 2022/23.

Stones and Silva will become the latest City legends to depart after Kevin De Bruyne, Kyle Walker and Ederson left last summer.

Stones: 'I lived all my dreams' at City

Image: Stones lifts the Champions League trophy after beating Inter

When announcing his departure on Instagram, Stones said: "It has been my home for the past 10 years and it will be my home for the rest of my life.

"It has been a rollercoaster in many ways. I came as a kid and now leaving as a man – becoming a father, a husband and, on the pitch, a very fulfilled player.

"I lived all my dreams out and lifted all the things that I came here to achieve.

"At the start of my career here I never would have thought I would be in this position. Firstly, to achieve everything but to have the love, the bond with everyone. Every dream has been smashed out of the park."

Guardiola praises 'adorable' Stones' influence

Image: John Stones with match-winner Nico Gonzalez at Wembley on Saturday

Stones made his first start for more than a month at Wembley against Southampton in the FA Cup semi-final because of injury issues keeping him from playing.

Guardiola made the defender captain for the 2-1 comeback win and was full of praise for his influence at City over the last decade when speaking about him pre-match.

Explaining his decision to bring Stones back into the XI, Guardiola told TNT Sports: "Finally, he has had three weeks or a month without injuries. Unfortunately, he had a lot in these last two seasons.

"He was our first signing when I arrived here. Difficult to understand the big success that we had without him, on and off the pitch. He is just adorable and a top player."

Sports.title: Sinner brushes Norrie aside in Madrid - and questions 'unusual' early start
Sports.content:
World No 1 Jannik Sinner recorded a routine 6-2 7-5 victory over British No 1 Cam Norrie to reach the Mutua Madrid Open quarter-finals.

Sinner won a sloppy 35-minute first set in which both players had more unforced errors than winners, breaking Norrie twice to put one foot in the next round.

The second set was a different story for the Brit, though, breaking back and holding serve against the Italian to take a 4-3 lead, but Sinner's quality eventually told, producing a crucial break at 5-5 and holding serve to take the match and secure an impressive round of 16 victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Round of 32 match between Jannik Sinner and Elmer Moller at the Madrid Open

The Wimbledon champion will face the winner of the round of 16 tie between the Czech Vit Kiprova and 19-year-old Madrid native Rafael Jodar in a bid to secure his first Madrid Open title and his ninth at ATP 1000 level.

It's not all bad news for Norrie, though, as he moves back into the world top 20 since 2024.

Image: Norrie is back into the top 20 despite his defeat

Sinner questions 'unusual' early start time

"The start time was quite unusual for me. I don't know when the last time I played at 11 was. For me it doesn't matter what time. I try to do my best," Sinner told the ATP.

"For me there was a question if me or Jodar plays at 4pm. I think it's right that he plays at 4pm. He finished very late. At the same time I think we need to make some adjustments with scheduling out the day.

"Two matches from 8pm is very late. Even though you have one day in between, but still it's very, very late. You finish at 1.30am. You need to eat.

"You need to have treatment. It's very late. But we try to adapt ourself, our bodies, and minds. From my side it was a good performance today."

Image: Jannik Sinner reacts after defeating Cameron Norrie at the Madrid Open tennis tournament

On beating Cam Norrie: ""We know each other quite well. We practiced a lot in the last tournaments also. We both kind of knew what to expect. I felt like I was serving quite well in important moments.

"This surface is very different than all the other surfaces. It's very tough to get the right feedback. Sometimes you feel like you're not playing your best but from the outside it seems like you are. Sometimes it's also the opposite.

"I'm very happy to be here in the quarters again. It's a tournament I haven't played a lot. So it means a lot to me. I'm happy to be through in two sets."

Sports.title: Man Utd in no rush to make managerial decision despite progress under Carrick
Sports.content:
With Manchester United all-but guaranteed Champions League football for next season, Michael Carrick has done all he can to get the head coach's job long-term. But United's bosses are in no rush, with a decision unlikely before the end of this campaign.

We can expect the hierarchy to talk to other possible candidates before making a final decision, such is the rigour that United will apply to their most important appointment. There will be a recruitment process, due diligence, strategic decision-making. Those are the buzz words of the new regime.

But while they might have sounded out other options via intermediaries, there have still been no formal meetings as yet. Again, the plan is to wait until the end of the season.

Under Carrick, United are 11 points clear of sixth place in the Premier League with 12 points left to play for. He was given one task when he took over on January 13: qualify for Europe's elite competition. It would need a spectacular collapse from here to miss out.

Manchester United

Liverpool Sunday 3rd May 2:30pm Kick off 3:30pm

However, the message coming out of Carrington seems to be 'no distractions until the football is done'. With bitter rivals Liverpool at Old Trafford on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, and the numerical possibility of United finishing anywhere between second and sixth in the table, there is still much to play for.

Appointing Ruben Amorim was clearly a mistake, but sacking him when they did in January, with 19 games of the season to play, was the right decision. United would not be where they are now if the Portuguese coach were still in charge.

It was clear that Jason Wilcox had become increasingly frustrated by Amorim's tactical inflexibility, as the director of football saw it. That flexibility was there for all to see in United's 2-1 victory over Brentford on Monday night, when the home side were repeatedly outplayed in the first half, conceding far too much space in midfield and as a result, far too many Brentford chances. Senne Lammens brilliantly kept Brentford at bay on at least three occasions.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester United and Brentford.

Carrick responded. He switched to a back-three at the break, tightened up the midfield, constricted the space, and effectively shut down the game in the second half. It made for a much less attractive spectacle, the Old Trafford crowd was becalmed, but it almost certainly helped United get over the line to claim another three points.

"Credit to them, they're a good team and have a really good mix of threats," Carrick told Sky Sports after the game. "We tweaked things second half and for the most part had decent control."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick is refusing to be drawn on whether he'll be made Manchester United boss beyond the end of this season.

That will have impressed his bosses for sure, but that alone does not mean he is a shoe-in for the top job long term. Carrick also maintains the best points-per-game (2.2) and goals-per-game (1.9) ratio since the Sir Alex Ferguson era.

He has done brilliantly in all aspects of the job since taking over, it's not just those statistics that standout. The way he has galvanised the squad coupled with the sure-handed way he has dealt with the media have impressed to the fullest. Just as important is the backing of the players, many of whom have come out in support of Carrick in recent weeks.

And practically, appointing Carrick would be a very smooth transition, making pre-season planning, transfer discussions and strategic preparation for next season much easier than bringing in someone from outside.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charlie Austin thinks Michael Carrick is the number one choice to be the Manchester United boss next season.

But United's bosses are mindful that the former United player has only had a very short time in charge (15 games so far) and that this season is likely to be pretty unique in United's history.

Out of both domestic cup competitions early and with no European football midweek, Carrick has had the luxury of preparing for just one game a week, with plenty of time with the players on the training pitch. No other United season, past or future, is likely to have so few matches. And that means the squad will inevitably be more stretched next season, whoever is in charge.

In many ways, United's bosses are in an invidious position, despite all the recent success. If they give the job to Carrick and results dip next season, there will be a chorus of voices chiming in to say the club has repeated the mistakes of the past, when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer started well but was ultimately sacked. Ironically, Sokskjaer was given the substantive job after a successful 15-game honeymoon, akin to where Carrick is right now.

But if the club were to bypass Carrick and bring in a big name, any failure next season would be met with criticism of the decision not to stick with a man who had done so well in the short term. Such is life at a club the size of Manchester United.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on his own podcast after Man Utd's win over Brentford, Gary Neville says Sunday's game against Liverpool is a huge game for both Michael Carrick and Arne Slot.

The reality is that, while Carrick has been performing well in the role, United's other options for the job have dwindled. Big names like Carlo Ancelotti, Thomas Tuchel, Julien Nagelsmann and Luis Enrique have been on their radar - coaches with the personality, experience and clout to cope with the scale of the role at Old Trafford.

But Ancelotti has signed a new contract with Brazil, Tuchel has done likewise with England, and it looks increasingly likely that Enrique will follow suit at PSG.

There is no doubt that Carrick is in pole position and few could argue he doesn't deserve it. It's clear, too, that there is a groundswell of support for him within the staff and players at Carrington training centre, a place he knows well, which is another big tick.

But this new, methodical Manchester United won't rush such a big decision. Whatever the clamour from outside, inside the corridors of power at Carrington, there is a quiet satisfaction with how things are going, and a determination to avoid the mistakes of the past.

Sports.title: Simeone confirms Arsenal interest in Alvarez
Sports.content:
Arsenal are interested in Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez but face competition to sign him from Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona, according to Diego Simeone.

The Atletico Madrid manager confirmed the interest at his press conference before the two sides meet in Wednesday's Champions League semi-final first leg at Metropolitano Stadium.

"I'm not inside Julian Alvarez's head," he said when asked about reports linking him with the Gunners.

"I understand it's normal that an extraordinary player like Julian Alvarez is wanted by Arsenal, Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona.

"It's normal because he's very good."

Alvarez has scored 48 goals in 104 games for Atletico Madrid since his £82m move from Manchester City, where he won back-to-back Premier League titles and was part of the 2022/23 treble.

The 26-year-old is known to Arsenal's sporting director Andrea Berta, who oversaw his move to Atletico from the Etihad Stadium.

Alvarez, who also won the World Cup with Argentina in 2022, has sat out of Atletico's last two games due to a minor injury but is expected to feature against Arsenal.

The Gunners added Viktor Gyokeres to their front line last summer but the former Sporting striker, their top scorer this season with 18 goals, was dropped in favour of Kai Havertz before the Germany international picked up an injury against Newcastle.

Sky Sports News understands Arsenal plan to be active in the summer transfer market and intend to add a forward, a central midfielder and a full-back.

Simeone aiming to make history

Like Arsenal, Atletico head into Wednesday's game hoping to win the Champions League for the first time in their history having reached the semis for a fourth time under Simeone.

"It's extraordinary that Atletico Madrid is in a Champions League semi-final again after nine years and after doing it for the fourth time in 14 years, if I'm not mistaken," he said.

Image: Atletico Madrid beat Spurs and Barcelona on their way to the last four

"That really is wonderful, it's incredible. And I think that faith, the excitement, the contagiousness that our people transmit to us will do us a lot of good.

"In terms of pressure, I don't feel the pressure and it is exciting to be as close as we are and we have never achieved it before.

"It is a special excitement. Leadership defines these games and we need to be ready and take the game to where we believe we can punish them. We will have a very tough game, against a fantastic rival and we are very excited about it."

Atletico were beaten 4-0 by Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium during the league phase in October and Simeone is wary of their dead-ball threat in particular.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eberechi Eze appears to have shaken off any injury doubts from the weekend

"We are going to face a tough game with a very good opponent and with a set-piece strategy that is very well worked," he said. "Let's go with all the excitement.

"I don't think football owes anyone anything. Things are deserved and achieved and for that you have to work and seek them, and obviously have luck behind you too."

Atletico captain Koke, whose contract expires at the end of the season, also expressed his excitement at the challenge ahead against Arsenal.

He said: "In the lead-up to these games, we are always excited. We feel butterflies in our stomach.

"It is just like a first date. Then once you start warming up it is all gone, it is just a football game, and you would be as excited as you would be for any semi-final.

"We expect a very strong Arsenal side and this is a Champions League semi-final and that is how we approach it."

Sports.title: Greaves for the Premier League? 'There is no ceiling - she's still getting better'
Sports.content:
What's next for brilliant Beau Greaves? The Premier League? "There is no ceiling - she's still getting better," claims Sky Sports' Laura Turner.

Greaves became the first woman to win a PDC ranking title with a historic 8-7 victory over Michael Smith in Monday's Players Championship 11 final.

The 22-year-old from Doncaster won seven straight matches in Milton Keynes which included a sensational deciding-leg victory with a 142 checkout over 'Bully Boy' in the showpiece to seal a landmark victory in darts history.

The two-time Women's World Matchplay champion took down a trio of former World Champions en route to the title, including Rob Cross, Gary Anderson and Smith in her final three matches of the event.

"I was glued to it," Turner told Sky Sports. "I'm sure she does feel pressure. She's human and she implied in her interview afterwards that she doesn't get to pull those 142 finishes off under pressure, but she doesn't show it.

"We all wax lyrical about how beautiful her throw is, it's so smooth but she uses it to perfection.

"She started to have deeper and deeper runs on the ProTour and there must have been some expectations because she's picked up a record 53 Women's Series titles since the middle of 2022, which is just unbelievable, but it's now transferring it to the next big thing.

"She's won on the Challenge Tour, Development Tour, and now she's won on ProTour, so I can see it happening, but for it to happen so quickly into her first year on the ProTour, that's something really impressive."

A catalyst for more titles

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Love The Darts panel discuss whether Greaves can win a major in darts, after her sensational start to life on the professional tour

Turner believes her victory on Monday will be a catalyst for winning more ProTour titles, despite Greaves admitting to being in complete shock.

"She's not doubting her ability because you have to put in performance after performance after performance at that level and she has maintained it," Turner said.

"Everyone is super proud of the progress she is making on the oche but she's a great person off it.

"I think there is no ceiling to what she can achieve because she's getting better and her goal now is to take what she's doing on the floor, keep maintaining that, and try and transition that onto the bigger stages."

The sky's the limit for Beau

Image: Greaves has landed a brace of nine-darters in 2026

The World Youth Championship runner-up has made a seamless adaptation to life as a PDC Tour Card Holder, and her latest breakthrough win takes her to within £4,000 of the provisional qualification spots for October's World Grand Prix - live on Sky Sports.

She has also landed a brace of nine-darters in 2026 - the most recent of those coming on the Development Tour on Friday.

"She's shown signs of being able to take her form to the next level on TV," said Turner. "I'm a big believer that when it becomes less scary she will start picking up more wins. How many deeper runs can she have? She's just won a ProTour title. The sky's the limit for her."

'A special, special talent'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Abi Davies and Chris Murphy discuss whether Greaves should be in the conversation for the Premier League

Speaking on Sky Sports News, Michael Bridge said: "If she carries on doing well in these ProTour Events she could qualify for some majors but nothing can stop her. The only person is herself because she has said she prefers playing against other women.

"She's absolutely dominated the Women's Series and now that she's won this it could really push her on to win more ProTour titles.

"She's a phenomenal player and I'm really looking forward to seeing how she gets on over the ProTour for the next few years.

"We had Fallon Sherrock winning matches at Alexandra Palace while Lisa Ashton won a Tour Card, but unfortunately during COVID it all had to stop. But we'll be seeing a lot more of Beau Greaves over the next few years. She is such a special, special, talent."

Greaves' shock at 'unbelievable' win

An emotional Greaves said after her victory on Monday: "I never thought I'd win one of these. Never, ever.

"I'm so happy. I can't even describe the way I feel. It's unbelievable and I feel so proud of myself.

Sports.title: ‘We are not happy’: Chiamaka Nnadozie on Wafcon debacle, boomboxes and Brighton
Sports.content:
Chiamaka Nnadozie has, at the age of 25, earned her place in the pantheon of African goalkeepers alongside legends such as Cameroon’s Thomas N’Kono and Morocco’s Zaki Badou.

Nnadozie featured at her first World Cup finals for Nigeria at 18, then played at the 2023 tournament and is the only goalkeeper to have won the Confederation of African Football’s (Caf’s) Golden Gloves award three times on the trot: in 2023, 2024 and 2025. Nnadozie, a reigning Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon) champion, is delighted and amazed that she has come so far, so quickly.

“I’m very surprised,” the Brighton player says of that three-in-a-row record. “I never knew I was the only one, but it’s a morale booster for me. People only see the success, but they don’t see the hard work behind it. But it’s thanks to my coaches and my teammates. It was from a collective effort that one was able to achieve those things.”

Music and football are inseparable for Nnadozie, the undisputed DJ of the Super Falcons. During last year’s triumphant Wafcon campaign in Morocco, she always had a boombox on her shoulders as she strolled into the training grounds in Casablanca and Rabat, with music from the Afrobeat superstars Wizkid, Davido, Rema and Burna Boy (the England coach Sarina Wiegman’s favourite artist) piping hot from the speakers.

“If I’m not carrying that boombox, the players will beat me up,” she jokes. “It’s always on me to make sure I bring the music. It keeps us moving, it gives us the morale … I love to be happy. When I’m happy, you get the best of me. That boombox is like my happiness, you know? We lost the boombox in Morocco. We forgot it inside the bus when we were going to the airport. We have a new one now.”

Nnadozie and Nigeria were supposed to be gunning for a record 11th Wafcon title in Morocco between mid-March and early April, before Caf postponed the tournament until July and August. “We, the players, are not happy about it,” she says bluntly. “We don’t know the reason behind it … we were all prepared. We left our clubs, hoping to go to the Wafcon. I know the fans are angry, the people are angry. It’s frustrating for me too because some of my family members already got their tickets, some had already applied for a visa.”

Nnadozie, though, remains positive about the growth and future of the women’s game in Africa, with Wafcon expanded to a 16-team event in which there will be a tournament debut for Malawi, who have arguably two of the best players in the world, the Chawinga sisters, Tabitha and Tenwa, the NWSL’s most valuable player.

View image in fullscreen Chiamaka Nnadozie is optimistic about Brighton’s prospects. ‘We know we need to work harder, but we’ll get there.’ Photograph: Graeme Robertson/The Guardian

“Women’s football [in Africa] is growing … [but] there’s this thing they always used to say: the universe isn’t on a budget. We can always ask for more.”

Nnadozie, speaking at Brighton’s training ground, has been adjusting to the Women’s Super League and the ambience of the Sussex countryside, a world apart from the glitzy Parisian metropolis where she spent time with Paris FC before moving to England last summer.

“I was convinced to join Brighton because of the way the coach spoke to me. The first time he saw me, he told me: ‘I watch you a lot. I like your qualities, and we think we can use that in this team.’ He explained how they want to work, how they work and what they want to achieve … that caught my attention.

“It’s good to know that I have people here that always tell me: ‘Chi, if you ever want to talk about anything, if you ever need to tell us anything, know it’s an open place where you can come express yourself, express how you feel.’”

Brighton are sixth in the WSL with three matches to play, well off a top-three finish which would deliver a Women’s Champions League place. But Nnadozie is hopeful of a bright future for the club and last Saturday’s stunning 3-2 home win over the leaders, Manchester City, was a positive pointer. “We know we need to work harder, but we’ll get there,” she says. “I believe in my teammates – each and every one of them.”
